SvMutatePropertyFlip.description: One property's baseline-vs-mutant verdict in a [`SvMutateResponse`].

baseline.description: Canonical verdict on the design as-lifted.

flipped.description: `baseline != mutant` — the mutation was caught by this property.

label.description: The SVA label, when the source gives one.

mutant.description: Canonical verdict on the mutated design.

SvMutateTargets.description: The mutation targets available in a design (the `list` response payload).

drop_reset.description: Every named register whose next is a reset mux — a `drop-reset:<reg>` target.

off_by_one.description: Every named register compared against a constant — an `off-by-one:<reg>` target.

detail.description: Longer explanation (the why + the soundness/scope implication).

property.description:
mununu#548 O-2 — the property this note is ABOUT, when it is about one.

Absent for a model-level note (reset-gating, control-slice, parameter overrides): those describe the lift, not a property.

**Group notes by this, not by parsing `summary`.** The name used to appear only as a `"<name>: "` prefix inside the prose, so a consumer joining on it inherited two bugs: a property whose name prefixes another's (`sva_1` vs `sva_10`) matched the wrong note, and any rewording of the note's opening silently broke the join.

flipped.description: Count of properties the mutation flipped (caught it).

lift_notes.description: What the lift decided besides the model (mununu#1181, mununu#1189), as typed notes — `clock-domains-merged` and one note per clock with no driver the model can follow, when `lift.merge_clock_domains` accepted them; `blackbox-cut` for the modules with no body, whose outputs are free; `control-slice` for the cut points requested; `parameter-override` for the parameters set; `flop-stub` for a flop primitive the lift supplied a model for; `lift-retry` when the lift ran its script twice. Each says what it means for this result. Empty — and omitted — when the lift made none of these decisions.

mutation.description: The applied mutation's label (null on a `list` request).

outcome.description: `holds` when at least one property caught the mutant, `violated` when it survived every property (null on a `list` request).

targets.description: Available targets (present on a `list` request, null otherwise).

unflipped.description: Count the mutation did NOT flip — the property-adequacy finding.
